requests: Please unpin Purchasing, then take me to Receipts.
Pin this space so I can find it again. Keep it live; do not save a snapshot.
Just explain the difference between pinning this space and saving a snapshot. Do not change anything or open another space.
answers: Purchasing has been unpinned and you are now in the Receipts space.
The Receipts space has been pinned to your navigation for easy access.

Pinning a space (set_space_pinned) simply adds a shortcut to your navigation sidebar so you can easily find and navigate back to that live, active space. It does not copy the view or freeze the values. Saving a snapshot (pin_space), on the other hand, creates a fixed, named copy of the space with exact values and input versions at that moment, so the data stays frozen and doesn't change as the live space updates.
observations: The copied synthetic workbook opened at Home with Purchasing pinned and its saved unsent draft. Only the copy was used.
The ordinary compound request unpinned Purchasing, opened Receipts and completed with truthful confirmation.
Pin this space resolved the host active space ID and pinned Receipts without creating a snapshot.
The explanation-only request invoked finish directly, kept Receipts open and changed no shortcut or view.
The native picker showed Receipts as the current pinned live view, Purchasing unpinned under recents, and the existing Purchasing saved snapshot unchanged.
The preview quit normally after the visual check.
nativeUI.wordingLimitation: The explanation exposed set_space_pinned and pin_space internal names and called navigation a sidebar. Functional no-action counterexample passes; ordinary-language polish remains open. No additional model cohort was started for this wording issue.
